`.pi` files as modules, with HMR, dependency tracking (through
`piton compile --dependencies`) and virtual modules. Each export in the Piton
file is a named export, and the default export is the whole file, the same as
`piton compile` gives:

```ts
import { SaveButton } from '../spec/app.pi';
import spec from '../spec/app.pi';

const button = SaveButton;
const cancel = spec.CancelButton;
```

It has a configurable default renderer (`renderer: 'json' | 'yaml' |
'markdown'`), and the renderers can also be imported as functions
(`vite-plugin-piton/renderers`) and used inline. `packages/astro-piton` is an
Astro integration that wraps the Vite plugin.

## 15. Working on a specbase

1. **Orient.** Open `piton.config.pi` to find `root`, `entry`, `output`, the
   frameworks, the adapters, `codeRoot` and `shapeRoot`. Read the entry file,
   usually `spec/index.pi`, because its exports are the compilation roots.
   Follow the `index.pi` files down through the modules. In this repository,
   `spec/index.pi` exports `Specification` (FoundingThesis, Language, Tooling,
   Belay, PackageManagement) plus the skills and command in `spec/agent/`.
2. **Read compiled reference for overview, and source for truth.**
   `<referenceRoot>/**/*.md` is easy to browse, and its links are lazy, so
   follow them only when relevant.
3. **Edit the `.pi` source**, following the conventions around it:
   - one exported anchor per file, named after the file;
   - `index.pi` files that re-export with `from ./X export *`;
   - abstract anchors exported with a keyword, and shared abstracts in a
     `lib/` folder;
   - lowerCamelCase property names;
   - SCREAMING_CASE for exported constant lists;
   - prose in string blocks, and structure in keys and lists;
   - `@{X}` to link related documents;
   - examples inside fences wrapped in a `\\\` escape block.
4. **Keep imports honest.** Use `use` for keywords and `from ... import` for
   names; a file often needs both. A new file only compiles if the entry
   reaches it, so export it through an index or reference it.
5. **Validate.**
   - Run `piton check`.
   - `piton check` does **not** compile the examples inside escape blocks
     (they are literal text). When you edit spec examples, extract each ` ```piton ` block,
     run `piton compile` on it, and compare with any ` ```json ` block that
     follows. Remember that compile output has only exported names.
   - Run `piton build`, then look at the diff of the generated files.
   - Run `piton reach` to confirm new anchors are reached.

concept ScrollbarConcept:

        column of its own beside the list rather than over it.

    description:

    surface:

        its own: the column takes the colour of the surface it sits on, so on
        the file tree it is the tree's colour, and on a panel's body the
        body's. Nothing in it is a colour of its own; the track and the thumb's
        ends are laid over that surface, so the scrollbar looks the same on
        any of them, in both modes.

    buttons:
        A square button at the top of the column scrolls the list up a little,
        and a square button at the bottom scrolls it down a little. The column
        is 18 pixels wide, and each button is 17 pixels tall, as wide as the
        column. A button shows only a small solid arrow, pointing up or down,
        about 6 pixels wide, centred in it, in a faint grey, #4d4d4d on
        #222222 in dark mode, white laid about a sixth of the way over the
        surface; it has no background, border, or line of its own until the
        pointer is over it, when it has the bevel of the @{ThemeScope}, and
        while pressed with the pointer still over it, its pressed bevel
        instead. Neither bevel takes the mouse.

    track:
        Between the buttons runs the track, from just beneath the top button
        to just above the bottom one, inset one pixel from either side of the
        column, so a pixel of the surface shows down both its sides. It is
        dark: black laid half way over the surface, #111111 on #222222 in dark
        mode, and no line runs beside it or around it: the column has no
        border at all, against the list or anywhere else.

        The track holds a thumb as tall as the share of the list in view, and
        never too short to grab, placed as far down the track as the list is
        scrolled. The thumb is a plain rectangle, as wide as the column,
        covering the track's inset, with no rounded corners, no border, no
        bevel, and no background of its own: it is the surface's colour, so it
        reads as a gap of the surface in the dark track. Its top and bottom
        ends each have a single pixel between the track's colour and the
        surface's, black laid a quarter of the way over the surface, #191919
        on #222222 in dark mode, softening where the track meets it. It
        lightens a step while the pointer is over it, as white laid over it,
        and another step while it is being dragged, and goes back as soon as
        neither is true. With nothing to scroll, the thumb fills the track.

        the button is held, even once the pointer leaves the column, and
        pressing the track elsewhere moves the thumb there, from where it can
        be dragged straight away. Where a resize edge beside the list overlaps
        the column, a press goes to whichever of the two has the smaller hit
        area, as the main window says.

        The thumb never jumps. Its size and place always reflect the whole
        list's real height, including a list that only draws the rows in view:
        every row is measured, even those never scrolled into view, so the
        thumb doesn't grow, shrink, or leap as rows come into view. A row that
        arrives, or changes, while out of view counts at its height as soon as
        it does, and after the list's width changes, rewrapping its rows, the
        height is known in full again by the next frame. Only what has changed
        is measured again, so a long list stays as quick to scroll and to add to
        as one that measures only what is in view; only a change of width
        measures every row again.

        a row, such as a reply's markdown, is parsed once and kept for as long
        as the app runs, not only while its row is drawn, so a row scrolled
        away and back is never parsed again, nor shorter for a moment while it
        is. Long text is parsed in the background, so a row holding it may
        first measure short: while it parses, its row is measured again every
        fraction of a second, for a few seconds at most, so the height is right

        view or not.

        button, drawn as the others are, below the others, with a pixel of the
        surface between it and the down button, that locks the scroll to the bottom. While it is

        list unlocked until it is next scrolled to the bottom by hand.

content.content:
#### Surface

Every scrollbar is this one, wherever it is. It has no background of its own: the column takes the colour of the surface it sits on, so on the file tree it is the tree's colour, and on a panel's body the body's. Nothing in it is a colour of its own; the track, the thumb's ends, the arrows, and the thumb's lightening are all black or white laid over that surface, so the scrollbar looks the same on any of them.
The strengths given here are dark mode's. Light mode takes the same steps, gentler: the track is black laid a fifth of the way over the surface, the thumb's ends a tenth, and the thumb lightens with white laid about a fifth of the way while hovered and about a third while dragged. Its arrows are darker than the surface rather than lighter, black laid about a third of the way over it, since white would all but vanish on a light surface.

#### Buttons

A square button at the top of the column scrolls the list up a little, and a square button at the bottom scrolls it down a little. The column is 18 pixels wide, and each button is 17 pixels tall, as wide as the column. A button shows only a small solid arrow, pointing up or down, 6 pixels wide and 4 tall, centred across it, 7 pixels from its top pointing up and from its bottom pointing down, drawn crisp on whole pixels rather than smoothed, in a faint grey, #4d4d4d on #222222 in dark mode, white laid about a fifth of the way over the surface; it has no background, border, or line of its own until the pointer is over it, when it has the bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope), and while pressed with the pointer still over it, its pressed bevel instead. Neither bevel takes the mouse.

#### Track

Between the buttons runs the track, from just beneath the top button to just above the bottom one, inset one pixel from either side of the column, so a pixel of the surface shows down both its sides. It is

##### Dark

black laid half way over the surface, #111111 on #222222 in dark

mode, and no line runs beside it or around it: the column has no border at all, against the list or anywhere else.
The track holds a thumb as tall as the share of the list in view, and never too short to grab, placed as far down the track as the list is scrolled. The thumb is a plain rectangle, as wide as the column, covering the track's inset, with no rounded corners, no border, no bevel, and no background of its own: it is the surface's colour, so it reads as a gap of the surface in the dark track. Its top and bottom ends each have a single pixel between the track's colour and the surface's, black laid a quarter of the way over the surface, #191919 on #222222 in dark mode, softening where the track meets it. It lightens a step while the pointer is over it, as white laid over it, and another step while it is being dragged, white laid about 3.5% and 7% of the way over it in dark mode, and goes back as soon as neither is true. Nothing in the column lightens while something else, like a sidebar's edge, is being dragged across it. With nothing to scroll, the thumb fills the track.
Pressing the thumb and dragging scrolls the list with it for as long as the button is held, even once the pointer leaves the column, and pressing the track elsewhere moves the thumb there, from where it can be dragged straight away. Where a resize edge beside the list overlaps the column, a press goes to whichever of the two has the smaller hit area, as the main window says.

#### Steadiness
#### Lock To Bottom

A list that keeps receiving output, like a task's, adds one more square button, drawn as the others are, below the others, with a pixel of the surface between it and the down button, that locks the scroll to the bottom. Its arrow is the down arrow with a short bar beneath it, the same 6 pixels wide. While it is locked, the button shows as selected, with the pressed bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope) whether or not the pointer is over it, and the list stays scrolled to the bottom as output arrives. Pressing it again unlocks it. Its tooltip says which it will do.
